Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reporter circled the Facebook/Twitter share icons in the file row of the Mixdrop page mxdrop.click, which the AdGuard Social Media filter did not hide. A domain-scoped element-hiding rule for those two anchors validated in the reporter's own settings profile:⁠ the icons are gone, no residue, page intact. ## Rule `mxdrop.click##.s-wrapper > .sc` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a social widget (Facebook/Twitter share buttons) and matches the stated purpose of the AdGuard Social Media filter, which blocks social media widgets such as Share buttons on third-party sites; the icons are not part of the site's functionality such as comments or social login. No policy rule in the run instruction closes it:⁠ it is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, not an anti-adblock wall, and not a scam/phishing page. Site traffic is not a blocking concern for this widely used file-hosting platform family that already has rules in the repository. ## Place in the list [SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/0cbe282a7b179745c082e2d570fc4e9d4b110538/SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"cb99c89671a9a41735df7710b73f9dee7411cc3075a87c93cdd9f7645bfe2c50"} -->
The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

The banner the reporter circled on nove3cinco.pt is the site's own first-party ad inventory:⁠ a publisher-hosted sponsor carousel (div#⁠banner, slides linking to froiz.pt and six other advertisers) with creatives on nove3cinco.pt's own uploads and no ad network request anywhere in the page's traffic. The repository policy that the site's own first-party advertising is not deliberately blocked therefore calls for recommending close rather than a rule.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction filter policy:⁠ "The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing." The reporter-defined target is a first-party ad served by the publisher itself, so the fix is blocked by this rule rather than by missing evidence. KnowledgeBase filter policy (served via lookup_rule_guidance):⁠ "The site's own advertising should not be deliberately blocked. However, it should not be unblocked if the blocking is caused by general filtering rules." A dedicated rule for this banner would deliberately block it; the banner is not blocked by any general rule today (get_applied_rules shows only four Tracking Protection scriptlets acting on the page). The report is not anti-adblock, not a paywall and not a scam/phishing page, so none of the other policy bullets applies; only the first-party-advertising bullet governs it.

## Artifacts

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reporter's screenshot shows an unlabelled Amazon Music promotional card in the right sidebar of the tomshw.it article; it is a third-party iframe from music.amazon.it/embed carrying affiliate parameters (irpid, ircid, iradid). Live evidence in the reporter's own settings profile confirms it, and EasyList Italy (defaults_plus_required comparison) does not cover it either. The proposed element-hiding rule hides that embed on tomshw.it; the browser experiment verified the ad disappears, no layout residue remains and the article is intact. ## Rule `tomshw.it##iframe[src^="https://music.amazon.it/embed/"]` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is an advertising complaint (label T:⁠ Ads) about a third-party Amazon affiliate/promotional embed served from music.amazon.it with affiliate tracking parameters (irpid, ircid, iradid), not the site's own first-party ad creative:⁠ the repository already treats Amazon offer units on tomshw.it as removable (tomshw.it#⁠%#⁠//scriptlet('json-prune-fetch-response', 'components.[⁠-]⁠.snapshot.[⁠=]⁠./www\⁠.amazon\⁠./', '', 'livewire/update') and tomshw.it#⁠#⁠div[⁠wire\⁠:⁠snapshot*="offer"]⁠). Not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock wall and not an anti-adblock gate at all, so none of the instruction's close-without-rule cases applies. ## Place in the list [ItalianFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/0cbe282a7b179745c082e2d570fc4e9d4b110538/ItalianFilter/sections/specific.txt) Next to the site's existing rules, before [line 45](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/0cbe282a7b179745c082e2d570fc4e9d4b110538/ItalianFilter/sections/specific.txt#L45). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported "Please disable your ad blocker to continue." notice on upfilesgo.com could not be reproduced:⁠ it never renders on the loaded page with the reporter's filters, and the download-button click that triggers it is refused by the sandbox, so no phase can reach the reporter's step. Analysis is handed over with the detector for the gate and an unverified neutralizer candidate for human review.

## Candidate for review

`upfilesgo.com#%#(()=>{let v;Object.defineProperty(window,'vhit',{configurable:true,get(){return v},set(o){v=o;try{Object.defineProperty(o,'detectAdblock',{configurable:true,get(){return()=>!1},set(){}})}catch(e){}}})})();`

BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt

Not verified: The reported symptom could not be observed in any phase. With the reporter's filters the notice never renders on the loaded page (DOM text search and full-page vision both show it absent), and the step that makes it appear — clicking form#⁠free-download-form button#⁠link-button-free after the five-second countdown — is refused by interact_page with refusalReason "publication", which also makes it unavailable to apply_rule revealSteps. apply_rule therefore returned environmentExperiment "inconclusive" (errorKind baseline_symptom_absent, validationSkipped true) and never judged the rule. Supporting (not validating) evidence:⁠ the repo's existing neutralizer, scriptlet('set-constant','window.vhit.detectAdblock','noopFunc'), produces no hit in the engine log and the live /_v/s.js function remains the site's real obfuscated detector, so this rule re-implements that intent as a trap on window.vhit that survives the site assigning the object.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Missing information

- No route to rehearse a symptom triggered by a download/publish control that interact_page refuses: The reported symptom ("AdGuard detected ... upon clicking the final download button") requires clicking form#⁠free-download-form button#⁠link-button-free on https:⁠//upfilesgo.com/zQe8. interact_page refuses that click with refusalReason "publication" (executedSteps 0), and apply_rule's revealSteps uses the same step grammar, so no phase can ever reach the page state the reporter describes. The run instruction says nothing about how to reproduce a symptom behind a control the sandbox classifies as unsafe, so the anti-adblock notice could not be produced, observed, or validated in any phase.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/43551374188

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"59b978ee61defb79255b9bd8fdaf0e2f72152207bdc36285082f6404bcc8cfac"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reporter's blank "adv space data-preview-ad" band under the header is real and caused by a `[data-preview-ad]` wrapper that keeps a fixed 287px height after the inner `.ad-frame` slot is hidden; hiding it closed the band with page integrity intact, but the vision review kept rejecting every candidate because it also treats the page's own empty 300px sidebar grid track as the same symptom, and that space cannot be cleared without deleting the site's "Caffè Scorretto" promo. No rule was verified, so this run reports the analysis and the low-risk rule `unionesarda.it##[data-preview-ad]` (ItalianFilter/sections/specific.txt) for human review.

## Still visible after the rule

- Per approfondire list / article body, right-hand column beside it (below the 'Un po' di calma' CaffèScorretto box seen at the top of tile 1) — The full-height right-hand ad rail (about 300 px wide, from the column divider at x≈1222 to the container edge) is completely blank white beside the article text and the 'Per approfondire' list. No ad creative, ad label, frame, divider or placeholder block is rendered anywhere in the column, yet the column keeps its reserved ad width/height for the whole length of the article. This is the reporter's 'companion blank reserved ad column' repeating below the header band.
- Right-hand rail beside the lower multimedia article list — Blank reserved right-hand ad rail/column; a vertical divider/frame is visible but no ad creative or label is rendered in it. This matches the companion blank reserved ad column described by the reporter.
- Right-hand rail beside the ARTICOLI CORRELATI grid — Blank reserved right-hand ad rail/column continues beside the related-article section; the divider/frame is visible, but the reserved ad space contains no creative or ad label.
- Right-hand rail beside the related-article grid and above the footer — Blank reserved right-hand ad rail/column continues through this tile with a visible divider/frame and no rendered ad creative.
- Right-hand rail beside the lower-page multimedia row above the footer (Quartu / Massimo Zedda / Violenza di genere) — Blank reserved right-hand column alongside the multimedia cards, bounded by the page's thin vertical column rule and containing no ad creative or ad label. This matches the reported empty right-rail advertising space.
- and 1 more of the same, in the run artifacts

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Missing information

- Reporter's language filter "AdGuard Italian" (id 26) is not resolvable in the locked filter baseline: The issue's reporter settings import lists `regular_filters=2,3,4,17,18,19,20,21,22,26`, where 26 is "AdGuard Italian" (the language filter that holds this Italian site's rules, e.g. ItalianFilter/sections/specific.txt line 252-255 for unionesarda.it). The locked environment's filterBaseline reported `skippedSources: [{kind: "unresolved_name", reportedName: "AdGuard Italian"}]`, and the reporter-profile launch answer's enabledLists contained only filters 2,3,4,17,18,19,20,21,22. Consequently no session in this run could apply or validate against the exact list the reporter had enabled; I fell back to repository search_rules hits for ItalianFilter to inventory that site's existing rules, and to a `defaults_plus_required` session (which loaded id 10 and EasyList Italy id 109 instead) for the controlled comparison. If exact reporter-list baseline is required for parity, the Italian filter source needs to be resolvable in the fixed environment.

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — shii4u.media (Arabic streaming site, shahid4u clone family) shows a centered anti-adblock modal asking visitors to disable their ad blocker, and locks the page body (inline overflow:⁠hidden) so nothing below the fold can be reached. Its inline detector fires from the blocked Google ad script; a scriptlet that stops the blocked script's onerror handler was verified in the reporter's AdGuard Browser Extension MV3 configuration (gate gone, page intact, no scroll lock). ## Rule `shii4u.media#%#//scriptlet('prevent-element-src-loading', 'script', 'pagead2.googlesyndication.com')` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale No run-instruction rule closes this report:⁠ it is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, and not a German anti-adblock wall — the page is Arabic and the wall itself reports the ad blocker. It is another anti-adblock wall, and the requests captured in the reporter session show the detector's script request (https:⁠//pagead2.googlesyndication.com/pagead/js/adsbygoogle.js?client=ca-pub-xxxx, blocked, artifact:⁠har:⁠69c258b3-ef00-47ba-a17e-0b741ea7216b) whose error handler creates div.ignielAdBlock, so a rule may be written. The wall aggressively withholds use of the site:⁠ it overlays the carousel and sets body overflow:⁠hidden, so the filter policy's anti-adblock criteria are met. A verified candidate exists, so the outcome is a rule proposal rather than a close or hand-off. ## Place in the list [BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/0cbe282a7b179745c082e2d570fc4e9d4b110538/BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 2174](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/0cbe282a7b179745c082e2d570fc4e9d4b110538/BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt#L2174). ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On joybuggy.com/pl a first-party "Witamy" cookie-consent dialog (ToS checkbox, "Akceptuj wszystkie"/"Tylko niezbędne"/"Ustawienia") is drawn over the storefront and no list hides it; it also appears with the controlled defaults profile, so it is a gap in the Cookie Notices filter rather than a configuration artifact. The domain-scoped element-hiding rule joybuggy.com#⁠#⁠[⁠data-testid="onboarding-modal"]⁠ was verified by apply_rule (symptom resolved, page intact, no residue). ## Rule `joybuggy.com##[data-testid="onboarding-modal"]` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie-consent notice, not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, and not an anti-adblock wall; the run instruction's policy rules therefore do not close it. Filter policy for the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter states that in most cases simply hiding the corresponding element or blocking its scripts is sufficient, which is what this rule does. No existing rule covers joybuggy.com and no shared rule family matches the banner, so a new domain-scoped rule is the appropriate form. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/0cbe282a7b179745c082e2d570fc4e9d4b110538/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/43556708910 Automated analysis against filters at `0cbe282`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reporter's annotated blank band is the leftover of birgun.net's unfilled `[data-section="ad-slot-belowhero"]` ad slot (343x280 px, min-height 280 px from the site's CSS, empty because the slot's fill request `||birgun.net/api/Ads/AdsGetList` is blocked by the AdGuard Turkish filter), and a domain-scoped hide removed it with page integrity intact. Both candidate experiments were nevertheless rejected by the vision review for large blank bands deep in the page's dynamically appended "next content" feed, where no ad element occupies height at all, so no candidate could be verified and none can be carried under the run's contract.

## Still visible after the rule

- Document y=5868..6680, between the article date/font-size controls and the police photo — A large blank white band roughly 280 px tall spans the article column between the date/font-size controls and the following photo. No ad creative, REKLAMA label, frame, or placeholder block is visible in it, consistent with a residual unfilled ad slot.
- Article body, between the paragraph ending “...gerçekleşmeden biliyorduk” dedi.” and the uppercase heading “HER ŞEYİ BİZ YAPTIK GEREKİRSE HER YERİ YIKARIZ” — A visibly oversized blank white vertical band spans the article column between the paragraph and the following uppercase heading. It is much taller than the normal paragraph spacing and shows no ad creative, label, frame, or placeholder block, matching a residual empty ad slot.
- between the paragraph ending “...cezaevine gönderiyorlar” and the heading “AYNI KOĞUŞA KONULDU” — A large blank white band spanning the article column sits between the body copy and the “AYNI KOĞUŞA KONULDU” heading. No ad creative, REKLAMA label, frame, divider, or placeholder block is visible in the gap, so it reads as reserved/unfilled ad-slot whitespace.
- Above '19 KASIM'DA HAKİM KARŞISINA ÇIKACAK' heading, below embedded quote ending at https:⁠//t.co/JS8W7blvu — A large blank white band spanning the article column, visibly taller than ordinary paragraph or heading spacing, appears after the embedded quote/link and before the next section heading. No ad creative, REKLAMA label, frame or placeholder block is visible, consistent with an unfilled ad slot.

## Reproduced symptom

m.youtube.com report:⁠ the complained-of item is an ad inside YouTube's own video player (sometimes preceded by a black player screen), i.e. the site's own first-party advertising, which the run's filter policy says must not be deliberately blocked and for which the report recommends closing. The reported flow itself could not be observed because YouTube served a sign-in bot-verification prompt in place of the player, so this is a policy-blocked recommendation, not a claim that the ad is gone.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction filter policy:⁠ "The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing." The reporter's complaint is an advertisement that plays inside YouTube's own video player on m.youtube.com, delivered into that player by the site operator's own ad infrastructure, so it is the site's own advertising. Linked filter policy document (AdguardTeam/KnowledgeBase filter-policy.md), Limitations and exceptions:⁠ "The site's own advertising should not be deliberately blocked. However, it should not be unblocked if the blocking is caused by general filtering rules" — no new blocking rule and no unblocking exception is warranted. None of the instruction's other branches applies:⁠ the page shows no ad-blocker detection wall (the only interstitial observed is a sign-in bot-verification prompt), it is not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock message, and not a scam/phishing/malware page. The existing shared YouTube handling is not extended here:⁠ get_applied_rules shows the Base-filter YouTube ad-placement scriptlet/json-prune family already acting on m.youtube.com, so this report adds nothing to that family. <!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"8c4ae722be13938af7ad36391410569827a73089e4279b7644409c6021432999"} -->
The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

The annotated element is Ukrainska Pravda's own in-feed newsletter signup block ("УП Ранок"), first-party self-promotion with no third-party ad request behind it, so policy gives first-party advertising no rule. The repository already hides this exact element with pravda.com.ua#⁠#⁠#⁠articles-container ⁠> div.article_news_list:⁠has(⁠> section[⁠id^="ranok_subscribe_"]⁠) in AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt, which the reporter's filter set does not include — recommend closing, no ad-filter rule should be added.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction policy, verbatim:⁠ 'The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing.' The reporter-annotated element is Ukrainska Pravda's own newsletter promotion (УП Ранок / 'Ежедневная новостная рассылка "Украинской правды"', 'Ваш email' field, 'Подписаться на рассылку' button):⁠ first-party, server-rendered markup (data-ranok-subscribe-form / data-ranok-email / data-ranok-visitor-id) with a first-party logo asset https:⁠//www⁠.pravda.com.ua/up/i/ranok.svg and no third-party ad request behind it in the HAR. That is the site's own advertising of its own product, so no ad-filter rule is generated. The repository's filter policy states 'The site's own advertising should not be deliberately blocked'. Every filter in the reporter's set (1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9, 13, 16, 23, 224) is an ad, tracking or language filter, so the only rule that could reach this reporter would deliberately block the site's own advertising there — which the policy forbids. No gap is left open by this decision:⁠ the repository already hides exactly this element with pravda.com.ua#⁠#⁠#⁠articles-container ⁠> div.article_news_list:⁠has(⁠> section[⁠id^="ranok_subscribe_"]⁠) in AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt line 398, and that selector matches the live DOM (it returns the 251px div.article_news_list wrapper that holds the block). The reporter's configuration simply does not include the Annoyances filters.

## Artifacts

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reporter's annotated leftover is the caption "If you like this file, share with your friends:⁠" on sharemods.com's second download page, whose share buttons the Social Media filter removes; that page is only reachable by a POST gated by a Cloudflare Turnstile that never renders in this browser, so its markup could not be inspected and no selector could be validated. I carry a domain-scoped, text-anchored hiding candidate for SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt for a human to confirm against the live second page.

## Candidate for review

`sharemods.com#?#p:has-text(If you like this file, share with your friends:)`

SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt

Not verified: The annotated element only exists on sharemods.com's second download page, which this session cannot load:⁠ the first page's form POST requires a Cloudflare Turnstile token, the widget never renders (0 iframes, empty cf-turnstile-response) and clicking #⁠downloadbtn returns 'Wrong captcha' without navigation (interaction-rehearsal-4, desktop and mobile profiles). Structured full-page vision of the reachable page reports the annotated caption absent (instanceCount 0), matching the DOM check, so apply_rule's cosmetic probe would match nothing and the element's tag/classes could never be inspected; the selector is anchored on the caption text the reporter's red box frames, with the element tag inferred, and may need widening to the whole share-block container if that block keeps reserved spacing. comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — campertrader.de shows a first-party Quasar cookie-consent dialog (.c-cookie-consent, "Wir nutzen Cookies - Aber warum?", fixed over the bottom of the Wohnmobil listings). The domain-scoped element-hiding rule campertrader.de#⁠#⁠.c-cookie-consent was lint-free to write and verified in the A/B/C experiment:⁠ the dialog is present before and gone after, with the listing page and its scrolling intact. ## Rule `campertrader.de##.c-cookie-consent` ## Policy rationale Run instruction:⁠ only the site's own advertising, paywalls and German anti-adblock walls close without a rule; this is a cookie-consent notice (T:⁠ Annoyance), the reporter's declared type, and the page shows no adblock detection (antiAdblockDetected false in every phase). The AdGuard Cookie Notices filter policy permits hiding a cookie notice when hiding is sufficient:⁠ the consent dialog is not gating content (75 listing images and all listing data already load) and the page has no scroll lock, so element hiding resolves the symptom without repairing a gated function. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/5b04336205d4eb0c186f551a8e428df60d486c40/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/43580670703 Automated analysis against filters at `5b04336`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — www⁠.caravana.de/wohnmobil shows its own first-party cookie-consent overlay (`.mmcm-container`, "Cookie Einstellung" with accept/reject buttons) over the listing page, and no published list handles it. Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reported annoyance on kfzversicherungsvergleich1.de is an iubenda CMP cookie banner (#⁠iubenda-cs-banner) loaded from the third-party hosts cs.iubenda.com and cdn.iubenda.com, which no enabled list covered for this domain. Extending the existing shared iubenda family with `||cs.iubenda.com^$domain=kfzversicherungsvergleich1.de` was verified:⁠ the banner is gone, the page stays intact and nothing else is hidden. ## Rule `||cs.iubenda.com^$domain=kfzversicherungsvergleich1.de` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie-notice/CMP annoyance (reporter comment 'cookie', screenshot shows only a German cookie consent dialog), not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, and not a German anti-adblock wall:⁠ the dialog carries no ad-blocker detection or allowlist demand. The AdGuard Cookie Notices filter is documented as blocking cookie notices and cookie-management-platform requests, so a rule belongs in this filter. Shared vendor families for iubenda already exist in AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt, and the maintainer guidance says to add the reported domain to such a shared rule rather than write a separate one. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/5b04336205d4eb0c186f551a8e428df60d486c40/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 294](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/5b04336205d4eb0c186f551a8e428df60d486c40/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L294). ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — wirkaufendeinauto.at shows a first-party GDPR consent modal ("Wir verwenden Cookies") that dims the page and locks scrolling via `html.modal-open`; hiding it would leave the page locked, so the fix clicks through the site's own consent flow and saves the selection with optional cookies declined, as the sibling wirkaufendeinauto.de rule already does for the same banner component. Browser validation with the reporter's filter set verified the rule:⁠ modal, dimming and scroll lock gone, page integrity intact, no remaining instances. ## Rule `wirkaufendeinauto.at#%#//scriptlet('trusted-click-element', '[data-qa-selector="gdpr-banner-configuration-button"], [data-qa-selector="gdpr-banner-accept-selected-button"]')` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie-consent notice (annoyance), the category the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter handles; the policy's no-rule rules cover German anti-adblock walls, paywalls and the site's own advertising, none of which applies here. The page shows no anti-adblock detector and no paywall; the gate is the site's own GDPR consent mechanism, and the fix completes its flow with non-essential cookies declined, as the Cookie Notices filter policy prescribes. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/5b04336205d4eb0c186f551a8e428df60d486c40/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reported cookie banner on www⁠.gebrauchtwagen.at is AutoScout24's own as24-cmp consent overlay (div#⁠as24-cmp-popup), and the repository already hides that same element for six sibling AutoScout24 sites without listing gebrauchtwagen.at. The domain-scoped rule gebrauchtwagen.at#⁠#⁠#⁠as24-cmp-popup was verified in the locked CLI baseline - overlay visible before, gone after, page intact - and the host merges it into the existing shared rule. ## Rule `gebrauchtwagen.at###as24-cmp-popup` ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie-consent notice, the exact class of annoyance the repository's AdGuard Cookie Notices filter is built for; it is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, not an anti-adblock wall, and not a scam page, so none of the instruction's close-or-hand-off rules applies. Network evidence identifies the site's own as24-cmp consent loaders behind the banner, and the element is already handled for sibling AutoScout24 sites, so a shared-rule extension is the right fix. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/5b04336205d4eb0c186f551a8e428df60d486c40/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 7989](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/5b04336205d4eb0c186f551a8e428df60d486c40/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L7989). ## Screenshots

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — kotsch.tech shows its own cookie-consent wall ("Cookies &⁠ Datenschutz", "Nur notwendige" / "Alle akzeptieren") over a blurred page while html/body keep scrolling locked, which AdGuard Cookie Notices does not clear. Declining non-essential cookies through the site's own "Nur notwendige" action removes the wall and unlocks the page, so kotsch.tech#⁠%#⁠//scriptlet('trusted-click-element', '.consent-necessary') was proposed and verified in the before/after experiment with the page left intact. ## Rule `kotsch.tech#%#//scriptlet('trusted-click-element', '.consent-necessary')` ## Policy rationale The run instruction closes first-party ads, paywalls, German anti-adblock walls, other anti-adblock walls without a captured detector script, and scam/phishing pages. This report is a cookie-consent notice (issue comment "cookie", screenshot of a "Cookies &⁠ privacy" consent modal), none of those rules applies, and no anti-adblock detection was observed on the page. The AdGuard Cookie Notices filter explicitly exists for cookie notices and CMP requests, and its policy prefers declining non-essential cookies by default, which the candidate does through the site's own "Nur notwendige" action. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/5b04336205d4eb0c186f551a8e428df60d486c40/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

comment.body:
<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"6a99ab73e38966526def675ef313bb0e81abef66c237e59ff7eba3ac27da4921"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported 'Adblock detected' wall on techwithia.com did not render in the locked AdGuard CLI baseline:⁠ three homepage loads plus an article page show no modal text, no fixed overlay beyond the site's sticky sidebar, no ad containers and normal scrolling, though the page does request Google Funding Choices message scripts and an unblocked first-party ad bundle on nfnasapz.techwithia.com. No rule could be validated, so the run hands a maintainer a candidate that adds techwithia.com to the existing ||fundingchoicesmessages.google.com^$domain=… anti-adblock family, noting that host also carries the site's TCF consent.

## Candidate for review

`||fundingchoicesmessages.google.com^$domain=techwithia.com`

BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt

Not verified: The reporter's modal ('Adblock detected', footer 'techwithai.com · powered by AntiAdblock Core') never rendered in the locked AdGuard CLI baseline:⁠ DOM text scans on three homepage loads (with 15 s of waits/scroll) and on an article page find none of its wording, no fixed overlay other than the sticky 'MÁS LEÍDOS' sidebar, and the page scrolls normally, so no phase could show it resolved. Full-page vision was inconsistent between batches (absent in one, generic blank spacing in another). The rule extends the existing anti-adblock family for this host (BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt line 609) because the captured requests (artifact:⁠har:⁠49c785d8-cfb5-4a88-8493-b2fd9cb4660f) contain only this third-party message platform, but it is unproven that it serves the reported modal and the same host also carries the site's TCF consent (__tcfapiLocator frame, FCCDCF cookie), so blocking it risks consent handling.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/43597339793

The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reporter annotated UNIAN's own share button at the right of the article meta row, but on the reported URL that widget (div.article__share-btn) is not rendered in any test session — its computed display is none, its icon is never requested, and full-page vision finds no instance — while the repository already hides that exact selector for unian.net in SocialFilter. No new rule is needed; recommend closing as not reproduced.

## Policy rationale

The run instruction's filter policy lists no rule that blocks this report:⁠ it is not first-party advertising, not a paywall, and not an anti-adblock wall; the report is a social-widget leftover, which is open to rule generation. The agent does not close issues; this propose_close only recommends closing for a maintainer's decision, with reproduction status not_reproduced.

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On footyheadlines.com an InMobi Choice consent modal (#⁠qc-cmp2-container, loaded from cmp.inmobi.com/choice/.../choice.js) covers and dims the homepage; the reporter's screenshot shows its "We value your privacy" variant. Blocking cmp.inmobi.com for this domain only removed the modal in the validated A/B/C experiment (visual review verified, no damage), so footyheadlines.com belongs in the existing shared ||cmp.inmobi.com^$domain=... rule. ## Rule `||cmp.inmobi.com^$domain=footyheadlines.com` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a consent/CMP overlay annoyance on the site's own page, not the site's first-party advertising and not a paywall, so the two closing rules do not apply. It is not a German anti-adblock wall (the page is not a German site's wall asking to disable the ad blocker) and not any anti-adblock wall; no detector request or 'disable your ad blocker' demand was observed, so the anti-adblock gate and human-review handoff rules do not apply. The captured network inventory shows the loader that renders the symptom (cmp.inmobi.com choice.js/cmp2.js/cmp2ui-en.js), and extending the existing shared vendor rule is the repository's documented way to handle a consent platform. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/f8744ff627a8b3caf83316a4a3ecc4227a05901a/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 114](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/f8744ff627a8b3caf83316a4a3ecc4227a05901a/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L114). ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reported annoyance on mdent-wroclaw.pl is the site's own fixed cookie-consent bar (".md-cookie":⁠ "UŻYWAMY PLIKÓW COOKIE" with "TYLKO NIEZBĘDNE"/"AKCEPTUJ WSZYSTKIE"), which no enabled filter hides. The domain-scoped rule mdent-wroclaw.pl#⁠#⁠.md-cookie for the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter was verified:⁠ the bar is hidden, the page stays intact and scrollable. ## Rule `mdent-wroclaw.pl##.md-cookie` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The run instruction's closing rules cover first-party advertising, paywalls, German anti-adblock walls and anti-adblock walls whose detector script was not captured; none applies here. The target is a cookie-consent bar, which the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists to hide, and the page's own requests show no anti-adblock detector. Repository policy on annoyance filters:⁠ the Cookie Notices filter blocks cookie notices on web pages; hiding the banner is sufficient here because no cookie decision is needed for the content the user reads (non-essential cookies are declined by default and the site falls back to a static map). Maintainer rule on popups/gates:⁠ a cosmetic rule that hides the popup is fine when the page then works — verified:⁠ the bar disappears with page integrity intact and the page keeps scrolling. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/6ba379da6343b4cca41235dd01da755f4799c4ad/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"adc12165881d84b78265a674cd2115b75eb7a18425a929be48ac602cec8edafb"} -->
The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

The circled filmibeat.com banner is first-party self-promotion:⁠ the creative is served from images.filmibeat.com and links to the site's own bigg-boss-20 topic page with its own campaign parameters, with no ad-network request behind it, while the page's real GPT/prebid ad slots are already blocked. Per the run instruction ("The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing") no rule is proposed and the report is recommended for closing.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction, Filter policy:⁠ "The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing." Run instruction, Filter policy, framing:⁠ "The agent never closes an issue. 'Recommend closing' below means the report says no rule is needed; a maintainer checks it and decides." Linked filter policy document (AdguardTeam/KnowledgeBase docs/general/ad-filtering/filter-policy.md), Limitations and exceptions for ad blocking filters:⁠ "The site's own advertising should not be deliberately blocked. However, it should not be unblocked if the blocking is caused by general filtering rules".

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/43600388865

The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported frankonia.de cookie-consent sheet ("Wer sagt schon \⁠"Nein\⁠" zu Cookies?", buttons "Ich stimme zu"/"Ablehnen"/"Einstellungen") does not reproduce on the loaded page:⁠ with the locked baseline the section .fr-c-message-wrap is display:⁠none and no consent overlay appears. AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt already carries frankonia.de#⁠$#⁠.fr-c-message-wrap { display:⁠ none!important; } (line 12074) plus frankonia.de#⁠$#⁠body { overflow:⁠ visible!important; } (line 12075) for exactly this element, so no new rule is needed. The reporter's iOS device showing it anyway could not be observed here and its cause remains unverified.

## Policy rationale

The run instruction's filter policy blocks rules only for first-party ads, paywalls and German anti-adblock walls; a cookie-consent sheet is none of these, so rule generation was allowed for this report. Rule generation was available but not needed:⁠ the repository's AdGuard Cookie Notices rules already cover the exact reported element, so no new rule was written.

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On the reported 048.ua AMP article the news grid leaves one-card-sized blank cells where unfilled AdSense <⁠amp-ad⁠> slots sit — the reporter's outlined blank column. The ad element itself is already collapsed/blocked, but its grid wrapper stays 320 px tall; hiding just those wrappers with 048.ua#⁠#⁠.card-wrapper:⁠has(⁠> amp-ad) removed all blank cells and the experiment verified with an intact page. ## Rule `048.ua##.card-wrapper:has(> amp-ad)` ## Policy rationale The reported defect is an unfilled advertising slot leaving blank layout space, not first-party editorial self-promotion, not a paywall, and not an anti-adblock wall, so no filter-policy rule blocks a fix. The site's own advertising is not being unblocked or deliberately blocked:⁠ the rule only hides an ad-slot container that renders no creative, which no existing list rule removes. Two existing multi-domain 048.ua cosmetic families (.banner, .popup-banner, .push-panel, .f-banner) and the general #⁠#⁠amp-ad rule do not cover the ad-slot wrapper, so a new domain-scoped rule is the smallest sufficient change. ## Place in the list [MobileFilter/sections/specific_web.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/15a5d423af5959fdd255738dc6bb95cebf1fd687/MobileFilter/sections/specific_web.txt) Next to the site's existing rules, before [line 3904](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/15a5d423af5959fdd255738dc6bb95cebf1fd687/MobileFilter/sections/specific_web.txt#L3904). ## Screenshots

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The kompas.com article loads and renders its content modules under the reported filter baseline (survey embed, KGNow video recommendation list, article text, embeds), and full-page vision reports the reporter's empty-panel symptom absent; the blank ad/player regions look the same across every session I could collect. No filtering rule in this repository could be tied to the reported breakage, so no rule change is proposed.

## Missing information

- No unfiltered control session and unverified reporter settings in the adguard_cli environment: For this incorrect-blocking report I needed an unfiltered reference page to see what filtering removes. In the locked adguard_cli environment every launch routes through the CLI proxy:⁠ launch_browser with extension "none" returned a session whose HAR still shows filtered requests (blockedCount 48, securepubads.g.doubleclick.net/tag/js/gpt.js, static.chartbeat.com, sb.scorecardresearch.com, go.rcvlink.com, local.adguard.org content scripts), so a true control page cannot be observed. Additionally the session launched with the issue's reporter import URL (reported_on_current) came back settingsVerified:⁠false with settingsEvidence:⁠null, so it is unknown whether the reporter's exact filter/stealth state was applied. Finally the accepted filterBaseline lists skippedSources for the reporter's third-party catalogs (Adblock Warning Removal List, Online Malicious URL Blocklist, AdBlockID, ABPindo, Frellwit's Swedish Filter), which are exactly the lists most likely to carry a kompas.com rule; no rule from them can be exercised. The run instruction does not say how such an unobservable control baseline should be reported.

The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — With the reporter's own filter selection the knowyourmeme.com article loads normally and the Admiral "Disabling Your Ad Blocker" wall never appears:⁠ the page's inline obfuscated Admiral snippet requests its detector from fourlevelsgame.com, and that request is already blocked by the existing ||fourlevelsgame.com^ rule in AdGuard Tracking Protection filter. The reported defect is not reproducible on current lists, so I recommend closing it rather than adding a rule.

## Policy rationale

The run instruction's filter policy closes German anti-adblock walls only; this is an English-language US site (knowyourmeme.com) whose page shows an English ad-blocker wall, so that rule does not apply and the report stays open to rule generation. The instruction's rule for other anti-adblock walls is satisfied and needs no new rule:⁠ the captured requests do show the detector script (https:⁠//fourlevelsgame.com/assets/ohtp0yf8m_ugz.min.js, appended by the page's obfuscated inline Admiral snippet) and it is already blocked by the existing ||fourlevelsgame.com^ rule of AdGuard Tracking Protection filter, so the wall never renders. The close rests on the reproduction status, not on a policy block.

## Artifacts

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — parakalsa.com shows a first-party cookie-consent banner fixed at the bottom ("Deneyimini iyileştirmek için çerezler kullanıyoruz" with "Sadece zorunlu"/"Tümünü kabul et") that the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter does not cover. A domain-scoped element-hiding rule anchored on the banner's own privacy-cookies link validated in the reporter's filter profile:⁠ banner gone, page intact, no remaining instances. ## Rule `parakalsa.com##div.fixed.inset-x-0.bottom-0.z-50:has(a[href*="#cerezler"])` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie notice, not the site's own advertising, not a paywall and not a German anti-adblock wall — none of the run instruction's closure rules apply. The page's network log shows no anti-adblock detector and no third-party CMP host; the banner is page-built HTML, so element hiding is the appropriate fix rather than a detector scriptlet or a vendor network rule. AdGuard Cookie Notices filter policy allows hiding cookie notices, and the page keeps working without the decision (content visible, no scroll lock), so no consent-state simulation was required. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/04e0f73b214ddc9d9c59ded9a5934878059d9f39/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/43620797508 Automated analysis against filters at `04e0f73`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

`bobswatches.com$$script:contains(BWConsentConfig)`

AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt

Not verified: apply_rule phase C removed the consent gate:⁠ .consent-overlay was visible in the baseline phase and not_found in the candidate phase, the candidate DOM shows <⁠html class="scroll-loaded"⁠> with no consent-open scroll lock, and the bound vision review reported symptom resolved, no remaining instances, no ad-layout residue and no observed damage. The reported reusable defect is an in-page promo popup (floating giveaway card overlapping the article margin), which the AdGuard Popups filter's stated purpose covers ('other types of popups that may annoy users'), and the repository already keeps such lenta.ru promo rules in AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/popups_specific.txt. None of the closing categories applies:⁠ no paywall, no German anti-adblock wall, no anti-adblock wall at all (antiAdblockDetected false, no detector request), and the symptom is not a scam/phishing page. The rule is DOM-only element hiding of one stable, domain-scoped class, verified by the experiment with the page intact, so the quality requirements (no performance cost, no over-broad reach) hold. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/popups_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/04e0f73b214ddc9d9c59ded9a5934878059d9f39/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/popups_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Missing information - No way to launch the reporter's settings-import profile in the locked adguard_cli environment: Issue #⁠247234 carries a reporter settings import URL (reports.adguard.com/settings/import.html?...product_type=win...), which the "Reporter settings profiles" section makes the reported_on_current profile that alone may verify a rule. In the locked adguard_cli environment the routing guidance says to launch every evidence session with extension:⁠"none", but launch_browser rejects that request with "A control session (extension \⁠"none\⁠") runs no blocker and takes no \⁠"settings\⁠"", while extension:⁠"prepared" belongs to the browser_extension environment. The run instruction and the environment descriptions therefore leave no documented route for running the reporter's imported settings under the accepted environment; validation ran instead against the CLI's own locked baseline, whose filterBaseline already contains every list named in the report (1,2,18,19,20,21,22) plus DNS, and which additionally applied the reporters' Stealth-mode-independent lists. The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

The reported ad reproduces:⁠ clicking play serves a first-party Kralbet spot in the player (plus a sponsored banner above it), fetched same-origin from diziizle.cloud's own /e/s and /e/b endpoints by the site's own player script. Under the run's filter policy ("The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule"), no rule is written and the report is recommended for closing.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

Run instruction, Filter policy:⁠ "The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing." The reported advertising is delivered first-party by diziizle.cloud itself:⁠ the in-player spot is fetched same-origin from https:⁠//diziizle.cloud/e/s, the banner above the player is fetched same-origin from https:⁠//diziizle.cloud/e/b, and both click through the site's own https:⁠//diziizle.cloud/e/g. The ad layer, skip countdown and 'Reklamı Aç' link are created by the site's own inline player script from a data-tbx config on its own player element ('src':⁠'/e/s','click':⁠'/e/g','skip':⁠5,'gate':⁠300,'freq':⁠'always'), i.e. self-served site advertising, not a third-party ad-network tag. No other filter-policy branch applies:⁠ the page is not paywalled, there is no anti-adblock wall on it, and the report is not a scam/phishing case. Per the run instruction the agent does not close the issue; this outcome recommends closing so a maintainer decides.

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — I proved live that telekom-security.com/de/ is scroll-locked because the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter hides the site's first-party consent overlay (`###cookie-container`, `##.cookie-content`) while the page keeps the overlay's inline `overflow-y: hidden` on `body`; my domain-scoped CSS rule releasing that lock was applied in the candidate phase but the vision review could not see relief, because this Chromium host paints no scrollbars (measured `innerWidth − clientWidth = 0`), so the fix reaches a human unverified.

## Candidate for review

`telekom-security.com#$#body { overflow-y: auto !important; }`

AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt

Not verified: apply_rule applied the rule (listed in phase C) but returned environmentExperiment "inconclusive" with no failedCandidateChecks; the vision review returned "rejected/not_resolved" (missing scrollbar) while pageIntegrity was "intact", adLayoutResidue "absent" and observedDamage empty. The symptom is unobservable here, not unresolved:⁠ this Chromium paints no scrollbars (measured:⁠ innerWidth - documentElement.clientWidth = 0), and a capture at scrollTop 0 cannot show a page became scrollable; interact_page scroll uses scroll-into-view, which also scrolls the locked baseline, so no discriminating reveal exists. Residual risk:⁠ on the reporter's Safari product CSS rules may not override inline styles.

## Still visible after the rule

- Top of page, right edge of viewport beside the hero 'WIR SIND SECURITY' (x≈1900, y=0–1080) — No vertical scrollbar track or thumb is rendered along the right edge of the viewport in this top-of-page tile, even though the document continues far below the first viewport. The right-edge strip is plain empty page background with nothing indicating scroll position or scroll availability, matching the reporter's 'scroll bar is gone' symptom for the first viewport of the page.
- Right edge of the viewport, running the full height alongside the hero banner, 'Mit Sicherheit zum Erfolg' section, and the 'Aktuelle Sicherheitslage und ihre Auswirkungen' heading — No vertical scrollbar track or thumb is rendered anywhere along the right edge of the viewport. The page is captured mid-document with content continuing below the bottom edge (the heading 'Aktuelle Sicherheitslage und ihre Auswirkungen' is cut by the frame), yet there is no scroll affordance, consistent with the scroll lock on body suppressing the scrollbar and preventing the rest of the tall homepage from being reached.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Missing information

- One-rule limit vs the repo's two-exception pattern for #⁠cookie-container / .cookie-content: The run instruction requires the outcome's rule field to contain exactly one filter rule, but this site's breakage is caused by TWO generic rules from `AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_general.txt`:⁠ `###cookie-container` (line 540) hides the consent wrapper and `##.cookie-content` (line 1304) hides its heading/text inside that wrapper. The repository's own established fix for this exact pair is two allowlist lines in `cookies_allowlist.txt` (e.g. `order.apexhotels.co.uk#@##cookie-container` line 1517 + `order.apexhotels.co.uk#@#.cookie-content` line 1518; `law.ed.ac.uk` lines 2135/2136). With a single rule an exception can only cancel one of the two, leaving a half-restored consent box, so the alternative single-rule fix (a `#$#` rule releasing the leftover `body` scroll lock) had to be chosen. Guidance on whether a multi-line "same-site pair" may ever be proposed would be useful.

- Empty white band immediately below the 'WIĘCEJ WIADOMOŚCI' statistics bar — Oversized blank reserved advertisement/recommendation band:⁠ a tall white area with no ad creative, recommendation cards, ad label, frame, divider or placeholder block visible. The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

The 'Reklama' area on podlaskieinfo.pl is the site's own ad slot:⁠ four first-party blocks (#⁠rek-4784-4 etc.) from its own "reklamy-manager" plugin, with creatives hosted on podlaskieinfo.pl and clicks through its own ?reklama_go= redirect, and no third-party ad request anywhere. The blank box under the label is that first-party slot's unfilled "miejsce na reklamę" placeholder (its images carry only data-srcset, so they never load), not a leftover caused by filtering, so repository policy blocks a rule and the report should be closed.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction filter policy:⁠ 'The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing.' Every ad on the reported page is the site's own:⁠ creatives hosted at podlaskieinfo.pl/wp-content/uploads/... , clicks through its own ?reklama_go= redirect, injected by its own reklamy-manager plugin; the HAR shows no third-party ad-network request. AdGuard filter policy (KnowledgeBase filter-policy.md):⁠ 'The site's own advertising should not be deliberately blocked.' A rule on .a-wrap/.reklama-inner/#⁠rek-* would deliberately block it. The reported blank box is the first-party slot's unfilled 'miejsce na reklamę' placeholder (images carry only data-srcset and are never requested) and is not a leftover produced by any blocked request, so there is no filtering defect to fix.

The repository's policy does not block content-access measures/paywalls, so no rule is proposed and the report should be closed.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

Filter policy, Limitations and exceptions:⁠ "Content access measures like paywalls are not blocked by Ad blocking filters. However, they may be blocked by Tracking protection filters if their operation results in a violation of user privacy" — the reported overlay makes article access conditional on consenting to personalised advertising/tracking or taking a paid Contentpass subscription. Run instruction filter policy:⁠ "Paywalls:⁠ no rule; recommend closing." The wall is a consent-or-pay variant of a paywall with no unpaid, non-consenting way to continue, so no rule may be written and the report is recommended for closing. The German anti-adblock clause does not apply:⁠ the page shows no ad-blocker detection or request to disable/allowlist the blocker (no detector script in the captured requests), so the page's German language and annoyance label are not grounds for a fix. The 'any other anti-adblock wall' clause does not apply either:⁠ no anti-adblock detector script appears in the captured request inventory, so this is not routed as an anti-adblock fix. The Cookie Notices filter's default-decline approach is unavailable:⁠ declining consent is itself the paid path here, and granting consent to personalised advertising/tracking on the user's behalf would defeat the extension's privacy function.

### Issue URL (Anti Adblock Script) [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/faa-ground-stop-canceled-flights-travelers-what-we-know/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.cbsnews.com%2Fnews%2Ffaa-ground-stop-canceled-flights-travelers-what-we-know%2F) ### Comment > ### Issue Description > Anti-adblock wall on `cbsnews.com` via Admiral First-Party Proxy. > > * **A/B Test Behavior:** Clean/Incognito sessions are served an inescapable hard wall with no dismiss link and page scrolling locked (`overflow: hidden`). Some regular sessions occasionally receive a variant with a delayed *"I'll fix it next time"* dismiss button. > * **Consent Requirement:** Only triggers after OneTrust (`cbsoptanon`) allows targeting/advertising cookies (`cmp.ot.targetingAllowed`). > > ### Proxied Admiral Script URLs Observed > * `https://silkyslumber.com/static/kmxtcpfvq/q1zxupa.js` > * `https://topicspin.com/static/k6vi91qgp/siqqoqasp4mu874ckh6569s5n2uum.js` > > ### Inline Bootstrap & Obfuscation Details > * Admiral's inline loader is wrapped in `loadAdmiralScript()` and invoked asynchronously inside `cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady` $\rightarrow$ `cmp.ot.targetingAllowed`. > * Because `loadAdmiralScript()` runs asynchronously after `document.currentScript` is `null`, inline scriptlets hooking `document.createElement` do not catch it. > * Evades generic Admiral signatures by aliasing `decodeURI` (`D(D(Y))`) and double-encoding `'admiral'` (`%25%36%31%64m%25%36%39%25%37%32%2561%6C`). > * Static Admiral Property ID in inline script: `QS01RDlDQzI1QTgyQ0FFMzUwNTQ5RkMwQUMtMg` > > ### Suggested / Verified Fix > Aborting synchronously when `loadAdmiralScript` is registered with `cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady` blocks Admiral before any proxied scripts are fetched: > ```adblock > cbsnews.com#%#//scriptlet('abort-current-inline-script', 'cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady', 'loadAdmiralScript') > ``` ``` Username: @SpoiledSneeze ``` ### Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — cbsnews.com serves an Admiral anti-adblock wall ("It looks like you're using an ad blocker." / VRM by Admiral footer, full-page dimmer, html+body overflow hidden) over an already-loaded article; the Admiral detector is loaded by an inline loadAdmiralScript() registered through cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady, with proxied Admiral scripts requested from topicspin.com and silkyslumber.com. The candidate scriptlet aborting that inline bootstrap was verified live:⁠ wall and scroll lock gone, page integrity intact, no remaining instances. ## Rule `cbsnews.com#%#//scriptlet('abort-current-inline-script', 'cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady', 'loadAdmiralScript')` ## Policy rationale The run instruction's policy for non-German anti-adblock walls is satisfied:⁠ the page's requests captured by the agent show the detector scripts (topicspin.com and silkyslumber.com Admiral proxy scripts in artifact:⁠har:⁠eb826755-f58d-4ae0-af87-60cfa678cadb), and the inline loader that registers them is present in the page DOM. The wall is not a German anti-adblock wall, not a paywall and not the site's own advertising:⁠ it dims an already-loaded CBS News article and locks scrolling, which the filter policy treats as effectively preventing use of the website. The maintainer rule 'Anti-adblock popups:⁠ hide the popup when that is enough' was considered first; a cosmetic hide would not release the html/body overflow lock and the wall's classes are randomized, so neutralizing the detector with a scriptlet is the appropriate form. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/antiadblock.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/04e0f73b214ddc9d9c59ded9a5934878059d9f39/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/antiadblock.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

### Issue URL (Anti Adblock Script) [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/faa-ground-stop-canceled-flights-travelers-what-we-know/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.cbsnews.com%2Fnews%2Ffaa-ground-stop-canceled-flights-travelers-what-we-know%2F) ### Comment > ### Issue Description > Anti-adblock wall on `cbsnews.com` via Admiral First-Party Proxy. > > * **A/B Test Behavior:** Clean/Incognito sessions are served an inescapable hard wall with no dismiss link and page scrolling locked (`overflow: hidden`). Some regular sessions occasionally receive a variant with a delayed *"I'll fix it next time"* dismiss button. > * **Consent Requirement:** Only triggers after OneTrust (`cbsoptanon`) allows targeting/advertising cookies (`cmp.ot.targetingAllowed`). > > ### Proxied Admiral Script URLs Observed > * `https://silkyslumber.com/static/kmxtcpfvq/q1zxupa.js` > * `https://topicspin.com/static/k6vi91qgp/siqqoqasp4mu874ckh6569s5n2uum.js` > > ### Inline Bootstrap & Obfuscation Details > * Admiral's inline loader is wrapped in `loadAdmiralScript()` and invoked asynchronously inside `cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady` $\rightarrow$ `cmp.ot.targetingAllowed`. > * Because `loadAdmiralScript()` runs asynchronously after `document.currentScript` is `null`, inline scriptlets hooking `document.createElement` do not catch it. > * Evades generic Admiral signatures by aliasing `decodeURI` (`D(D(Y))`) and double-encoding `'admiral'` (`%25%36%31%64m%25%36%39%25%37%32%2561%6C`). > * Static Admiral Property ID in inline script: `QS01RDlDQzI1QTgyQ0FFMzUwNTQ5RkMwQUMtMg` > > ### Suggested / Verified Fix > Aborting synchronously when `loadAdmiralScript` is registered with `cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady` blocks Admiral before any proxied scripts are fetched: > ```adblock > cbsnews.com#%#//scriptlet('abort-current-inline-script', 'cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady', 'loadAdmiralScript') > ``` ``` Username: @SpoiledSneeze ``` ### Screenshots

Some regular sessions occasionally receive a variant with a delayed *"I'll fix it next time"* dismiss button. > * **Consent Requirement:** Only triggers after OneTrust (`cbsoptanon`) allows targeting/advertising cookies (`cmp.ot.targetingAllowed`). > > ### Proxied Admiral Script URLs Observed > * `https://silkyslumber.com/static/kmxtcpfvq/q1zxupa.js` > * `https://topicspin.com/static/k6vi91qgp/siqqoqasp4mu874ckh6569s5n2uum.js` > > ### Inline Bootstrap & Obfuscation Details > * Admiral's inline loader is wrapped in `loadAdmiralScript()` and invoked asynchronously inside `cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady` $\rightarrow$ `cmp.ot.targetingAllowed`. > * Because `loadAdmiralScript()` runs asynchronously after `document.currentScript` is `null`, inline scriptlets hooking `document.createElement` do not catch it. > * Evades generic Admiral signatures by aliasing `decodeURI` (`D(D(Y))`) and double-encoding `'admiral'` (`%25%36%31%64m%25%36%39%25%37%32%2561%6C`). > * Static Admiral Property ID in inline script: `QS01RDlDQzI1QTgyQ0FFMzUwNTQ5RkMwQUMtMg` > > ### Suggested / Verified Fix > Aborting synchronously when `loadAdmiralScript` is registered with `cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady` blocks Admiral before any proxied scripts are fetched: > ```adblock > cbsnews.com#%#//scriptlet('abort-current-inline-script', 'cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady', 'loadAdmiralScript') > ``` ``` Username: @SpoiledSneeze ``` ### Screenshots

Some regular sessions occasionally receive a variant with a delayed *"I'll fix it next time"* dismiss button. > * **Consent Requirement:** Only triggers after OneTrust (`cbsoptanon`) allows targeting/advertising cookies (`cmp.ot.targetingAllowed`). > > ### Proxied Admiral Script URLs Observed > * `https://silkyslumber.com/static/kmxtcpfvq/q1zxupa.js` > * `https://topicspin.com/static/k6vi91qgp/siqqoqasp4mu874ckh6569s5n2uum.js` > > ### Inline Bootstrap & Obfuscation Details > * Admiral's inline loader is wrapped in `loadAdmiralScript()` and invoked asynchronously inside `cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady` $\rightarrow$ `cmp.ot.targetingAllowed`. > * Because `loadAdmiralScript()` runs asynchronously after `document.currentScript` is `null`, inline scriptlets hooking `document.createElement` do not catch it. > * Evades generic Admiral signatures by aliasing `decodeURI` (`D(D(Y))`) and double-encoding `'admiral'` (`%25%36%31%64m%25%36%39%25%37%32%2561%6C`). > * Static Admiral Property ID in inline script: `QS01RDlDQzI1QTgyQ0FFMzUwNTQ5RkMwQUMtMg` > > ### Suggested / Verified Fix > Aborting synchronously when `loadAdmiralScript` is registered with `cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady` blocks Admiral before any proxied scripts are fetched: > ```adblock > cbsnews.com#%#//scriptlet('abort-current-inline-script', 'cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady', 'loadAdmiralScript') > ``` ``` Username: @SpoiledSneeze ``` ### Screenshots

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"3a37207f5f0660b0e362bedc1404d92cf3a05d2030f7e7f551a65b8b87e062ce"} -->
The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

The arrows mark Recorded Future promo units on therecord.media (300x1050 sidebar and 970x250 in-article creatives) served from the site's own CMS and linking to recordedfuture.com on "The Record from Recorded Future News" — present in both the live page and full-page vision. That is the site owner's own first-party advertising, which the run instruction's filter policy gives no rule and recommends closing; a maintainer decides (the repository's self-promo section is recorded as a conflict).

## Policy rationale

Run instruction, Filter policy:⁠ "The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing." The reported promo is first-party self-promotion:⁠ both creatives are served from the site's own CMS (cms.therecord.media, HTTP 200) and link to https:⁠//www⁠.recordedfuture.com/?utm_source=therecord&⁠utm_medium=referral&⁠utm_content=post-sidebar-ad or post-footer-ad on a site whose own title is "The Record from Recorded Future News"; no third-party advertiser or ad network appears in the HAR. KnowledgeBase filter policy, Ad blocking filters ⁠> Limitations and exceptions:⁠ "The site's own advertising should not be deliberately blocked." The only other requests rules act on are Google Tag Manager and Matomo trackers, already covered by AdGuard Tracking Protection filter. Conflict recorded for the maintainer:⁠ this repository also keeps a dedicated self-promotion section (AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt, e.g. firstandgoal.ru#⁠#⁠.self-promo), and the KnowledgeBase gives the AdGuard Other Annoyances filter the purpose of blocking website self-promotion "if it is considered an annoying element". That alternate reading was not applied because the run instruction's own Filter policy governs this run and states no rule for the site's own first-party advertising; the maintainer makes the final decision. The target is reproduced, not absent:⁠ structured full-page vision of the proxied session reports reporterSymptomPresence "present" for the annotated promo units, so this is a policy decision, not a not-reproduced decision.

## Artifacts

The AdGuard Cookie Notices filter's purpose covers this kind of first-party consent bar, and no allowlist exception exists for the domain. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/04e0f73b214ddc9d9c59ded9a5934878059d9f39/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 6467](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/04e0f73b214ddc9d9c59ded9a5934878059d9f39/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L6467). ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — ctlan.ru serves a fixed bottom cookie-consent bar (`div#ccru-banner`) that no existing filter hides; the reporter's own filter set (executed as the AdGuard CLI baseline) still shows it. The domain-scoped hiding rule `ctlan.ru###ccru-banner` was verified in the before/after experiment:⁠ the bar is gone, the page is intact and no residue remains. ## Rule `ctlan.ru###ccru-banner` ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie-consent notice annoyance, which is not first-party advertising, not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock wall and not a scam page, so the run instruction's closing rules do not apply. The AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists for exactly this symptom class, and the rule is a simple domain-scoped element hiding rule. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/04e0f73b214ddc9d9c59ded9a5934878059d9f39/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/43647023774 Automated analysis against filters at `04e0f73`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — Reproduced arbital.ru's fixed Tilda cookie-consent card ('.t972__banner', 'Мы используем файлы cookie…') and verified that hiding it with the domain-scoped rule arbital.ru#⁠#⁠.t972__banner removes the notice with the page intact and no layout residue. The reporter's separate 'mobile app' mention was not present on the page; the rule is proposed for the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter. ## Rule `arbital.ru##.t972__banner` ## Policy rationale The report is an annoyance (cookie notice), not first-party advertising, a paywall, or an anti-adblock wall, so none of the run instruction's closing rules applies. AdGuard Cookie Notices filter policy:⁠ 'This filter is designed to block both cookie notices and requests from cookie management platforms (CMPs)' and 'In most cases, simply hiding or blocking the corresponding scripts is sufficient' — a domain-scoped hiding rule is the accepted fix. No existing rule covers arbital.ru or the Tilda block selector .t972__banner (domain inventory and selector searches returned 0 matches), so a new shared-family rule is not an option and a site rule is written. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/04e0f73b214ddc9d9c59ded9a5934878059d9f39/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reporter's "Google button" is a first-party "Freie Presse bei Google bevorzugen" promotion bar served in the article HTML (an <⁠a class="article__google-preferred"⁠> linking to google.com/preferences/source), with no request behind it and no existing rule matching it. The domain-scoped hide freiepresse.de#⁠#⁠.article__google-preferred was verified in the browser:⁠ the bar is visible before and gone after, with the page intact and no remaining instances. ## Rule `freiepresse.de##.article__google-preferred` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is an annoyance about a site engagement/self-promotion prompt, not the site's own advertising, not a paywall complaint and not an anti-adblock wall, so none of the policy's closing rules applies. The repository already maintains a generic rule for the same Google 'preferred source' widget type (#⁠#⁠.google-preferred-source in the Subscriptions - Generic section), which shows this class of widget is in scope. The widget is served in the page HTML with no distinct request behind it, so the fix is a domain-scoped element-hiding rule written and verified against the reporter-profile baseline. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/04e0f73b214ddc9d9c59ded9a5934878059d9f39/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/43645460102 Automated analysis against filters at `04e0f73`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"a3703d259ad9b646aceb69d5fa2aaa1fa28adff6c0fcbc80f6374cf357c5fb42"} -->
The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

On www⁠.17yoo.cn every third-party ad request (MediaV/360 splash, Baidu union slot) is already blocked in the reporter's exact filter configuration; the advertising that still renders — a popup banner with a '不再弹出' dismiss pill whose creative, ad-config and impression requests all come from the site's own hosts (engine.17yoo.cn, dsp-res.17yoo.cn, d.17yoo.cn) — is the site's own (first-party) advertising, which the run instruction's policy excludes from rule generation. Recommend closing with no rule.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

Run instruction policy:⁠ "The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing." The advertising still rendered under the reporter's exact filter configuration is served only from the site's own hosts — creative dsp-res.17yoo.cn/v1/upload/20250815/EmBQQfKOjq.jpg, ad config engine.17yoo.cn/v1/fa, impression d.17yoo.cn/dv.gif, all reported thirdParty:⁠false in artifact:⁠har:⁠9d4d8959-6445-4286-ba82-904c4be5ac28 — i.e. the site's own direct-sold ad inventory, matching the reporter's own wording that the unblocked ads are '自带的' (the site's built-in ones). All third-party ad traffic on the page is already blocked by existing rules (||mediav.com^$third-party…, ||cpro.baidustatic.com^, /cpro/ui/*), so there is no unblocked third-party ad left for a new rule to target. The run instruction states the agent never closes an issue and a maintainer decides, so this is a recommendation to close with no rule rather than an autonomous close.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/43654315374

<sub>Automated analysis against filters at `04e0f73`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.</sub>

### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking) [https://www.youtube.com/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2F) ### Comment > **Problem: YouTube playlist repeat switches off when AdGuard is enabled.** > > For approximately four months, YouTube's playlist repeat function has stopped working correctly in Google Chrome. > > When I enable repeat, it switches off when the next video starts. This happens across multiple playlists and on three different computers. > > I have updated AdGuard's filters, refreshed YouTube, and tested with another ad-blocking extension disabled. The problem persists. > > **Important test results:** > - With AdGuard enabled, the repeat function switches off between songs. > - With AdGuard disabled, repeat stays enabled across several songs, but YouTube advertisements appear. > - Screenshots showing both situations are attached. > > I have used AdGuard successfully for a long time, and YouTube's repeat function previously worked correctly. > > Please investigate whether an AdGuard filtering rule is interfering with YouTube's playlist repeat function. I would appreciate a solution that allows me to keep blocking advertisements while using repeat. ### Screenshots
